title: Atlasshift QBR - cost, reliability & roadmap sync
summary: Quarterly health review focused on unexpected inference cost spikes, two latency incidents in Feb, and roadmap alignment for a mid-year pilot of Redwood Dedicated. Agreed to run a 72-hour load test on a dedicated pool, share cost breakdowns, and schedule security scoping with infra team.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam Parker: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have Alex, Priya, Marcus, Samir from Atlasshift and Riya and Nadia here from Redwood. Quick check audio?
[00:09] Alex Chen: Audio's good.
[00:11] Priya Patel: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:14] Liam Parker: Great. Goal for today is a compact QBR-ish checkin — usage, a couple of reliability events you had in Feb, and the mid-year roadmap around Dedicated. We'll keep this to 45 minutes.
[00:28] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. We're keen to understand root cause for cost increases — our CFO pinged me.
[00:34] Riya Desai: Totally. We pulled the token-level billing and also your tail-latency histograms, so we can walk through.
[00:40] Nadia Ruiz: And we'll propose a pilot plan for Dedicated so you can see predictable throughput.
[00:45] --- Summary snapshot / auto notes (auto-generated, may be noisy) ---
[00:50] Topics: usage + costs, two latency incidents (Feb 3 and Feb 21), Dedicated pilot ask, SOC2/SSO/KMS questions.
[01:00] --- Transcript body ---
[01:02] Liam Parker: Okay Alex, can you describe what changed in Feb from your side? Any new features shipped or traffic patterns?
[01:12] Alex Chen: So we shipped the contextual summarization microservice on Feb 1st; that's when we saw the first rise. It's a lot more beam-type requests — longer prompts, more history. Also we toggled a high-temp mode for a subset of requests — small fraction but heavy token output.
[01:29] Priya Patel: On Feb 3 we saw a tail-latency spike, CPU not the issue, it was GPU queuing. Our logs show sudden burst of long seq lengths. There was some retry flood from client side too.
[01:41] Riya Desai: That aligns with the KV cache miss pattern we saw — prefix caching wasn't hitting because the prompt windows changed. We recommended enabling prefix caching live, but I know you were worried about staleness.
[01:53] Alex Chen: Right, our devs were wary about serving stale context, especially for the financial summaries.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: Also on costs — we saw a 38% month-over-month increase on February vs January. The big line items were generation tokens and retries.
[02:11] Liam Parker: We pulled the per-route cost heatmap — I'll share the sheet after the call — but short answer: the long outputs + retry amplification explains most of the delta.
[02:21] Samir Goyal: Could some of this be solved with model family change? We are on redwood-hosted gptj-style model now. Would switching to a quantized variant cut costs?
[02:31] Riya Desai: Potentially. We have quantized 4-bit variants for the same family that reduce per-token compute, but you tradeoff a small quality delta. For summarization, we can run a quick eval on your prompt set.
[02:43] Priya Patel: We care about output fidelity. If there's an eval harness, we'll run it — but our bar is pretty high, must match previous metrics within 2% for key precision metrics.
[02:53] Riya Desai: That's doable. We'll request your eval prompts and expected outputs.
[02:58] Marcus Lee: What about Dedicated — would that fix the latency spikes?
[03:03] Riya Desai: Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools so you won't suffer noisy neighbor bursts; autoscaling can be tuned to keep queue length under SLO. For the Feb incidents, Dedicated plus prefix caching would likely have avoided the queuing.
[03:16] Alex Chen: What's the commit size for Dedicated? We aren't ready for long-term capex-like commitments.
[03:21] Liam Parker: We have flexible reserved capacity for 3/6/12 months. There's also a burst buffer option so you can autoscale slightly above reservation for short peaks. We can model costs for you.
[03:32] Nadia Ruiz: We'll include a simulation of your Feb spike under hosted vs dedicated in the follow-up deck.
[03:38] --- Incident deep-dive (Feb 21) ---
[03:40] Priya Patel: The second incident Feb 21 was trickier — a downstream service in our pipeline started injecting longer context windows because of a bug. That caused the requests to balloon mid-day and our client started retrying after 1.5s timeouts which amplified the load.
[03:58] Liam Parker: Got it. So three compounding factors: code change, longer seq lengths, and retry amplification.
[04:03] Alex Chen: Right. The SRE playbook helped but we want to avoid recurrence. Any guardrails Redwood offers for automatic backpressure?
[04:11] Riya Desai: Yes — you can set per-route rate limits, concurrency caps, and dynamic fallback policies to a cheaper model when latency climbs. We also offer automatic prefix cache policy that evicts on staleness heuristics.
[04:24] Priya Patel: Where do we configure that? Console or API?
[04:27] Riya Desai: Both. Console for quick toggles and policy templates, API for infra automation. We'll show your team a policy template in the redwood console link.
[04:36] Marcus Lee: One security question — our compliance team insists on KMS integration and audit logs for model inputs. Are logs redacted by default?
[04:44] Liam Parker: We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated; for hosted, we have an encryption-at-rest model and optional tokenization/redaction pipelines. Audit logs are available but you can opt to mask PII. We'll hand over SOC 2 docs and our audit log schema.
[04:59] Alex Chen: Residency requirement — some accounts must keep logs in EU. Can Redwood store logs regionally?
[05:05] Nadia Ruiz: Yes, data residency is available as an enterprise option — either region-specific hosted endpoints or Private deployment. We'll add the region mapping in our follow-up.
[05:15] Samir Goyal: For the pilot, what would you recommend we test first?
[05:18] Riya Desai: I propose a 72-hour Dedicated pilot: mirror a subset of production traffic (10-20% synthetic mix), enable prefix caching, run quantized variant A/B for summarization routes, and capture latency/cost metrics. We'll coordinate a spike window to observe autoscaler behavior.
[05:33] Priya Patel: We need the ability to failover back to hosted mid-test if quality regressions occur.
[05:38] Riya Desai: Absolutely — Canary rollouts and automatic fallback are built-in. We'll configure canary thresholds so any QoQ drop triggers rollback.
[05:46] Marcus Lee: Cost modeling — how quickly can you produce the delta between hosted and Dedicated for Feb patterns?
[05:52] Liam Parker: We'll run the sim overnight and share a spreadsheet tomorrow. Expect a per-token compute delta + reservation amortized across your 72-hour pilot.
[06:00] --- Objections & tradeoffs ---
[06:02] Alex Chen: CFO will ask, if Dedicated needs a minimum commit, what's the break-even vs hosted — we need a clear number.
[06:10] Liam Parker: We'll include break-even analysis at multiple utilization points (40%, 60%, 90%). Also show sensitivity to retry rates.
[06:17] Samir Goyal: Is there any way to limit retries client-side automatically? We've got lots of internal retries from the microservice.
[06:24] Priya Patel: We're fixing client retry logic, but having server-side backoff hints would help.
[06:29] Riya Desai: You can emit 429s with Retry-After headers or enable connection-level throttling; those are straightforward in the config.
[06:36] --- Security & procurement notes ---
[06:38] Marcus Lee: Procurement wants a SOC 2 + ISO attestation and standard SLA. Also SSO for users.
[06:46] Liam Parker: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts; SSO via SAML is supported and RBAC provisioning through SCIM. We'll share the security pack.
[06:55] Priya Patel: Also we need to validate the audit log schema for legal hold requests.
[06:59] Nadia Ruiz: Noted — we'll include schema snippets and sample redaction configs.
[07:05] --- Action items check ---
[07:07] Liam Parker: I'll read out action items, please correct me if I mis-attribute.
[07:12] Liam Parker: Action item 1: Redwood to run cost simulation for Feb patterns hosted vs Dedicated and send spreadsheet (due: 2026-03-03).
[07:22] Liam Parker: Action item 2: Atlasshift to share eval prompt set and expected outputs for summarization (owner: Alex) (due: 2026-03-05).
[07:34] Liam Parker: Action item 3: Redwood SE (Riya) to configure a pilot plan including quantized A/B config and prefix cache policy draft (due: 2026-03-04).
[07:46] Liam Parker: Action item 4: Security pack (SOC2/ISO + KMS/residency notes) to be shared by Nadia (due: 2026-03-03).
[07:56] Liam Parker: Action item 5: Schedule 72-hour Dedicated pilot window — coordinate dates, propose March 9-11 tentatively (owner: Samir + Nadia) (due: 2026-03-04).
[08:09] Alex Chen: That all looks right.
[08:12] Priya Patel: Quick note — please include sample dashboards for tail-latency and per-route retries.
[08:18] Riya Desai: We'll include those. Also a runbook snippet for toggling fallback policies.
[08:24] Marcus Lee: On the pilot, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[08:28] Riya Desai: Log samples, eval prompts, and traffic mix. Also a short list of SLOs you want to target (p95, p99) and acceptable quality deltas.
[08:37] Samir Goyal: We'll pull that together.
[08:40] --- Closing recap ---
[08:42] Liam Parker: Recap — simulate costs tomorrow, security pack tomorrow, pilot plan and A/B configs by Thursday, and Alex to send eval prompts. We'll target pilot March 9-11 pending coordination.
[08:55] Alex Chen: Thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[08:58] Liam Parker: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the deck and links.
